0.comment: Overview — Tokugawa Restoration Labyrinth: Ooku (curated; based on public recaps, not verbatim game text)
0.content:
[Setting: Fate/Grand Order — "Tokugawa Restoration Labyrinth: Ōoku" (徳川回天迷宮 大奥), war 9080]
During the Lostbelt era, while Chaldea prepares its assault on the Atlantic Lostbelt, nearly all of Chaldea's staff and Servants suddenly vanish. Only Ritsuka Fujimaru, Mash, Sion, Parvati and Kiara remain. The cause is traced to a pseudo-singularity in mid-17th-century Japan: the Ōoku — the women's quarters of Edo Castle — transformed into a vast, many-layered labyrinth. The missing people were not abducted into the labyrinth after it formed; they were taken AS MATERIAL to build it, their "heat of existence" woven into its halls. The deeper the Master descends, the stronger the labyrinth's corrupting temptation becomes. (Originally ran March 27–April 10, 2019; revived July 22–August 5, 2020; now permanently available as a Main Interlude.)

1.content: The Ōoku (大奥, "great interior") was the innermost sanctum of Edo Castle: the shogun's women's quarters, home to his consorts and hundreds of female attendants under a strict hierarchy, established in the era of Tokugawa Iemitsu with Kasuga no Tsubone as its matron. Men other than the shogun could not freely enter. In this event, a replica Ōoku has been rebuilt as a supernatural labyrinth — endless tatami corridors, sliding doors that rearrange themselves, and an atmosphere thick with incense, luxury, and quiet menace.

2.comment: The Restoration Labyrinth — how it works
2.content: The Restoration Labyrinth (回天迷宮) is the Ōoku recreated as a descending, multi-layered maze. It was constructed from the existences of the kidnapped Chaldea personnel, Servants, and singularity remnants. Exploring costs Osuzu Paper Lanterns, spent to commit to a branch; progress reveals new branching spots and dead ends. Defeating Huge Ghost enemies along the way yields inrō — pillboxes each patterned after a historical Tokugawa shogun, treated in-story as condensed fragments of that shogun's soul, seduced and bound here by the labyrinth's mistress. Wielding their power both unlocks unique combat skills and slowly overwrites the Master's own self into "a Tokugawa", making them ever more susceptible to Kama's charm. The labyrinth is, in essence, a trap of indulgence: rest, pleasure, and surrender are always offered as easier options than walking on. Hanafuda cards found along the way tilt the final confrontation — white cards weaken the labyrinth's mistress, black cards strengthen her.

3.content: Kama (カーマ) is the Indian god of love, burned to ash by the third eye of Shiva and here manifested as an Assassin-class Servant in the body of a young girl (a vessel with Sakura's face, mirroring Parvati). In this incident Kama is fused with Mara (マーラ), the demon of temptation, and rules the labyrinth as its mistress. Her manner is teasing, languid, and razor-tongued — she offers comfort, pampering, and love without effort, and despises being refused. Beneath the mockery lies deep self-loathing: love was her duty, and love destroyed her. Her goal is to drown the world in indulgent, rotting love and claim the seat of Beast III/L — the counterpart to Kiara's Beast III/R. At the labyrinth's deepest level she swells into the gigantic Kama/Mara, fought as the event's climactic raid boss.

4.content: Parvati (パールヴァティー), gentle consort of Shiva, manifested as a Lancer pseudo-Servant in Sakura's body. One of the few left behind when Chaldea's people vanished, she becomes the Master's chief companion in the labyrinth. Kind, modest, and quietly resolute, she carries a personal wound into this incident: Kama — the god her husband's flame reduced to ash — is family to her household, and Kama's warped state is something she cannot look away from. She fights to stop Kama and, if possible, to reach her.

5.comment: Sessyoin Kiara — ally with an agenda of her own
5.content: Sessyoin Kiara (殺生院キアラ), the demonic bodhisattva, accompanies the party through the labyrinth. As the being who holds the seat of Beast III/R (Rapture), she is uniquely qualified — and unnervingly delighted — to commentate on Kama's nature. Serene, honeyed, and always faintly predatory, Kiara treats the whole incident as a fascinating mirror: Kama's smothering, decaying love (Lapse/Depravity) versus her own devouring lust. She is genuinely useful to the Master, yet no one ever quite relaxes around her. (Spoiler: late in the story Kiara throws herself away in a decisive act against Kama/Mara — by her own admission driven less by altruism than by sheer spite toward Mara, the other half she refuses to lose to.)

6.comment: Kasuga no Tsubone — guide within the labyrinth
6.content: Kasuga no Tsubone (春日局), wet nurse of shogun Tokugawa Iemitsu and the formidable matron who built the real Ōoku's institutions, appears within the labyrinth as a spirit bound to this false Ōoku. Formal, dutiful, and sharp-eyed, she guides the Master through the quarters' protocols and layers, lending the party legitimacy inside a place where outsiders — especially men — should not walk. Her loyalty to the Tokugawa house is absolute, which makes the labyrinth's abuse of the shoguns' souls a personal affront.

7.comment: Matsudaira Nobutsuna — the shogunate's side of the incident (kept deliberately vague; verify against transcripts)
7.content: Matsudaira Nobutsuna (松平信綱), called "Izu no Kami" and famed as the brilliant, coldly rational senior councilor of the early Tokugawa shogunate, is entangled in the labyrinth's origin on the shogunate's side of history. Within the false Ōoku his name and office carry administrative weight: the labyrinth's court treats Tokugawa authority as law, which the party can sometimes turn to their advantage. Treat the exact details of his bargain and fate as story spoilers to be confirmed from the actual transcripts.

8.content: Sion Eltnam Sokaris, the Atlas Institute alchemist aboard Novum Chaldea, serves as mission control for the Ōoku incident. With nearly everyone else converted into labyrinth material, her analysis is the party's only outside line: she tracks the labyrinth's structure, warns of its corrupting effect on the Master, and coordinates the descent toward its mistress.

9.content: Ritsuka Fujimaru, Chaldea's last Master, and Mash Kyrielight, the Shielder demi-Servant, anchor the party as always — but the Ōoku is a battlefield aimed at the heart rather than the body. The labyrinth courts the Master constantly with rest, luxury, and Kama's affection, and the shogun-souls the party must gather actively erode the Master's identity. Mash's steadiness — and her bluntly unimpressed reactions to the Ōoku's seductions — is one of the party's best defenses.

10.content: The Beasts are the seven great calamities born from humanity itself. The third seat is split in two: Beast III/R — "Rapture", the devouring lust embodied by Sessyoin Kiara — and Beast III/L, its opposite face of stagnant, smothering love and depravity, the seat Kama/Mara reaches for in the Ōoku incident. Where III/R consumes through desire that takes, III/L rots through love that gives endlessly until nothing moves. The two halves loathe each other: Kama and Kiara needle and snipe constantly, precisely because they are two faces of the same seat. The Ōoku labyrinth is effectively a nest built to hatch that Beast.

11.content: Nega-Desire (ネガ・デザイア) is Kama/Mara's authority as a Beast candidate: a field that nullifies and drains desire itself. Within it, drive, ambition, and fighting spirit leak away — in battle terms it empties the party's charge every turn; in story terms it is why the labyrinth makes intruders want to simply lie down and be loved. Kasuga no Tsubone's protection over the party's quarters is what keeps the Master's will intact deep inside the Ōoku.

12.comment: Osuzu Paper Lantern — map exploration resource (from the war map page)
12.content: The Osuzu Paper Lantern (御鈴行灯) is the exploration resource of the Restoration Labyrinth: spending one at a branch point commits the party to that path and reveals the next spot. Paper Lanterns are earned mostly by clearing dead-end routes, so a "wrong turn" is rarely wasted — it still pays out the resource needed to try a different branch. Faint hints are scattered through the labyrinth to help pick the route toward the depths rather than a dead end.

13.comment: Inrō — the event's signature item and Master Skill mechanic
13.content: The Inrō (印籠) is the event's signature item: a Tokugawa-crested pillbox obtained by defeating a Huge Ghost-type enemy encountered while advancing the story. Each Inrō is patterned after a specific historical Tokugawa shogun, and for the rest of the event it replaces the Master's usual Mystic Code skills with a unique "Inrō Skill" named for that shogun — one that only grows stronger as more Inrō are collected. Narratively this lines up with the labyrinth's core threat: each Inrō is treated as a condensed fragment of a shogun's soul that Kama/Mara seduced and bound into the Ōoku, and channeling that power is what slowly rewrites the Master's own self into "a Tokugawa" devoted to her.

14.comment: Event map structure (from the interactive war map page)
14.content: The event map renders the labyrinth as spots (nodes) pinned over a floor-plan background image, connected by drawn roads between the repeatable ("FQ") farming nodes. Clearing certain story spots causes several new spots to bloom onto the map at once, opening multiple branching routes at the same time — the player chooses which branch to commit a Paper Lantern to. Not every branch leads forward: some are dead ends, which is where most Paper Lanterns are recovered before doubling back to try another path.
